newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia says EU deal boosting foreign investment.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia says EU deal boosting foreign investment.

text.p: Tunisia said on Wednesday it was attracting more foreign investment since had it signed a free trade accord last year with the European Union.

International Cooperation and Foreign Investment Minister Mohamed Ghannouchi told a news conference that the value of planned foreign investment had increased by 90 percent since the accord was signed with the EU in July 1995.

The total amount of foreign investments planned mainly in the manufacturing and agriculture sectors was 506.5 million dinars ($491.3 million) from July 1995 to July 1996 compared to 266.5 million from July 1994 to July 1995.
"This is the first impact of the accord with the EU, and since then we are noticing an increasing interest from international groups for investment in Tunisia," he said.

The latest international group looking at Tunisia for making a possible investment was South Korean conglomerate Daewoo after a visit earlier this month by South Korean President Kim Woo Choong, he said.
"We are discussing some investment opportunities. We will announce the results when these discussions are finalised," Ghannouchi said without elaborating.

Direct foreign investment amounted to 2.132 billion dinars from 1992 to 1995. Nearly 87 percent of the amount went to the energy sector, and the remainder to tourism, manufacturing and agriculture sectors.
He said that during the same period, 623 firms were launched in the manufacturing sector financed by foreign capital, meaning there were now 1,600 foreign firms established in Tunisia.
In order to attract more foreign investment, the government planned to open 26 industrial zones, and to invest some 570 million dinars in training over the next seven years.
Measures to offer more opportunities for foreign investors to purchase shares in firms to be privatised through the Tunis Stock Exchange were planned, Ghannouchi said.
These measures include a larger stake for foreign investors in public share offers.
